instruction: Retire a merged branch immediately: tag it completed/<branch>@<date> so history stays recoverable, remove its worktree, delete the branch. Refuse when the worktree has uncommitted files. Never let residue accumulate.
outcome: A forced worktree removal destroyed a CERTIFIED verdict (L-11). Retiring on merge stops merged work being picked up again by accident.

instruction: Treat the main branch as production: build release artifacts only from main, and let nothing reach main without a full regression pass and an explicit go.
outcome: Hard constraint.

instruction: Never commit or push directly to main, agents included. Cut a branch for every feature or defect from an updated main (fix/<issue-id>-<slug> or feat/<slug>).
outcome: Hard constraint.

instruction: Follow a fixed release flow: branch -> dev build -> verify -> gate -> merge -> version bump -> tag -> release build from main -> push.
outcome: Hard constraint.

instruction: Ship the store artifact as the store bundle format, built from main and signed with the owner's upload key. Verify the signature and never ship a debug-signed or fat artifact.
outcome: Store requirements; details in .claude/rules/builds.md.

instruction: Version with a patch bump for defects and a minor bump for features; the build code must always increase. Tag the merge commit and push the tag.
outcome: Android rejects a non-increasing versionCode.

instruction: Never disturb the user's running devices or emulators: no wipe, reinstall-over, force-stop or data clear without asking, and never kill an emulator mid-session. Read-only inspection is fine. This overrides 'run autonomously'.
outcome: A fresh install destroys local state and forces a re-login.

instruction: Give every guard an explicit, reasoned escape hatch (e.g. '# guard-ok: <reason>', '--no-verify' with the reason in the commit message) and log every refusal and override.
outcome: A guardrail with no escape hatch gets disabled wholesale.

instruction: Retire a branch on merge: tag it completed/<branch>@<date>, remove its worktree and delete it. Refuse when the worktree holds uncommitted files. Never let residue accumulate.
outcome: A forced worktree removal destroyed a CERTIFIED verdict (L-11).

instruction: Treat main as production. Never commit or push directly to main (the assistant included). Branch every feature or defect from freshly pulled main as fix/<issue-id>-<slug> or feat/<slug>.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Follow the release flow in order: branch, dev build, verify, gate, merge, version bump, tag, production artifact from main, push.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Bump the patch version for defects and the minor version for features. The build number always increases. Tag the merge commit and push the tag.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Never disturb the user's running devices or emulators: no wipe, reinstall-over, force-stop or data clear on a device in use without asking, and never kill an emulator mid-session. Read-only inspection is fine. This overrides 'run autonomously'.
outcome: A fresh install destroys local state and forces a re-login.

instruction: When a safety classifier refuses a command, re-issue it in sanctioned form (no --force, no rm -rf, git -C instead of cd, one question per call) and relaunch from disk.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Adversarially self-review before every commit (what did you not test or assume?), then check the actual state with git status and git diff --cached. Never commit blind.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Install the repo's git hooks once per clone, and have session start set the hooks path. Hooks do not self-activate.
outcome: A doc row once said the SessionStart hook 'warns' when it actually installs, which made the guardrail sound optional.

instruction: Block commits that stage generated artifacts (code-graph output, build directories, review-tool output).
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Block commits of product code alongside a fix doc whose verification checkbox is unticked.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Keep the repo self-contained: no paths outside it, no submodules, no foreign framework material in scripts, configs, CI or hooks. Run a grep check whose any output means a dependency crept back.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Never edit, analyze or vendor a sibling framework repo during product work.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: If a production identifier move is genuinely intended, bypass the guard with a stated reason and a rollout plan for clients already in the field.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Tag a gated composition before removing anything.
outcome: A train that gated cleanly then found the checkout contended saved its work by tagging. An untagged detached commit is collectable.

instruction: Refuse the shortcut that looks like success.
outcome: A train declined to move main to its own merge, because the working copy would then read as a revert and the next commit would silently erase the merged rows.

instruction: Test only on disposable tenants or accounts. Never install over, write to or log into live production accounts or the devices that hold them, and re-check which devices currently carry live sessions.
outcome: An emulator's stored session was switched on-device to the live tenant (D364), so it inherited the never-touch rules.

instruction: No agent types a password, and no credential or PIN is ever written into a file or commit. Use a carried session or an out-of-repo autologin file; the setup script refuses to write inside the repo.
outcome: Session carry across a fresh install was proven at 21-23 s with zero owner logins.
enforcement: scripts/setup_dev_autologin.sh refuses an in-repo path; scripts/verify/session_carry.sh

instruction: Block staging of generated or tool-output directories (build output, dependency caches, code-graph output, external review-tool output) in a pre-commit check.
outcome: Guards against an external tool's output ever being committed; no incident numbers given.

instruction: Before committing, check the actual current state (git status, git diff --cached, re-read the files), because an earlier step may have changed something. Never commit blind on the assumption that a previous step worked.
outcome: Standing principle; no measurement given.

instruction: Install the repo's git hooks once per clone, because they do not self-activate. Have the session-start hook set core.hooksPath and make the pre-commit executable, and describe guardrail enforcement precisely (installs vs warns).
outcome: A doc row said the SessionStart hook 'warns' when it actually installs; corrected 2026-08-28 because the wrong wording made the guardrail sound optional. The hook never runs install.sh, so only pre-commit gets chmod-ed.

instruction: Block commits that stage paths outside the repo, env vars pointing at a sibling framework, absolute sibling paths, or a submodule file.
outcome: Prevents the vendored-framework divergence incident from recurring (see the standalone item).

instruction: Give hooks a deliberate escape hatch (--no-verify), because a guardrail with no escape hatch gets disabled wholesale; anyone who bypasses says why in the commit message. Keep the hook a thin wrapper over one policy script that CI also runs, so a bypassed hook is still checked.
outcome: A rule enforced only in a hook is on the honour system, since --no-verify skips every hook.

instruction: Keep the repo standalone. Never add a path outside the repo, an env var pointing at a sibling framework, a git submodule, or vendored copies of another project's material.
outcome: The repo once vendored a framework as ~338 tracked files plus a submodule; the copies diverged until the vendored one was 550 commits ahead of the standalone repo.

instruction: Treat production cloud configuration as frozen. Never change project, app or database ids, make additive edits only, and never regenerate config from another project or account.
outcome: Devices in the field still talk to those ids.

instruction: Stage bulk remote writes: batch them, throttle between batches, prefer a quiet window, dry-run first, and audit-log the original document bodies.
outcome: 3,837 unstaged deletes once stalled menu_items, users and tables on every connected till.

instruction: Tag a gated composition (a merge result) before removing or moving anything; an untagged detached commit is collectable.
outcome: A train that gated cleanly and then found the checkout contended saved its work by tagging it.

instruction: Refuse the shortcut that looks like success. For example, do not move a branch ref when the working tree would then read as a revert of what was just merged.
outcome: A train declined to move the main ref to its own merge: the working-tree copy would have read as a revert, and the next commit would have silently erased the merged rows.

instruction: A COMMIT step (2 min) stages only the named paths, writes the activity-log entry and commits.
outcome: One of the five allowed dispatch shapes.

instruction: Give every guard a sanctioned policy door so a legitimate action (such as a revert) always has a legal path.
outcome: The REQ-148 policy door unblocked a revert that had no other legal path; it paid in kind (unblocked vs blocked), not in speed.

instruction: Take test logins only from a session carry or a home-directory autologin file that is never in the repo. No agent types a password, and no credential or PIN is ever written to a file or commit.
outcome: Security rule.

instruction: Never edit or analyze a sibling framework repo during app work, and never vendor it back in.
outcome: The vendored-framework divergence (550 commits) is the incident behind this rule.

instruction: Never commit on the production branch. Branch first and merge with --no-ff. Never chain 'git checkout main && git commit': if HEAD is already on main the checkout is a no-op and the commit lands on production. Check 'git branch --show-current' before staging, not after committing.
outcome: Pointer lesson. A direct non-merge commit on main fails the policy.
enforcement: POLICY 11 in scripts/policy_check.sh (section at :1114); merge door recognised by MERGE_HEAD in .githooks/pre-merge-commit:17-18

instruction: An uncommitted artifact is not evidence. Before merging a branch or removing a worktree, run 'git -C <worktree> status --short' and commit or rescue every modified or untracked file that is part of the deliverable (verdicts, ticked boxes, measurement files). 'git worktree remove --force' destroys unstaged work irrecoverably. Never assert an outcome in a merge message that the merged tree does not carry.
outcome: Pointer lesson (owner: orchestrator). Earned by a merge that asserted CERTIFIED over a tree that did not carry the verdict.
enforcement: scripts/pipeline/complete_branch.sh:47-50 (skips a worktree with M/??/A entries); scripts/verify/branch_health.sh refuses to stamp a dirty worktree

instruction: Stage EXPLICIT PATHS. Never 'git add -A <dir>' while other agents are writing there. If a sweep is unavoidable, run 'git status --short' first and account for every entry before staging.
outcome: Happened twice on 2026-08-28 (Recurrences: 1). A half-written REQ-043 analysis was swept in and caught by POLICY 9c. REQ-064-design.md landed inside a commit titled for REQ-059, so it was invisible in history. The commit history lied.

instruction: The shell's working directory persists across tool calls. Never 'cd' into another worktree; address it with 'git -C <path>'. Print 'pwd' and 'git branch --show-current' in the same call before any checkout or commit. A destructive git operation from an unverified cwd damages a running agent's evidence silently.
outcome: A persisted cd made 'git checkout -b ... main' switch a worktree off the branch while a Test Agent was certifying it. Results from that window would have certified the absence of the change. It was detected only because a later command failed loudly.

instruction: Never type multi-step merges inline from a cd'd shell or behind an output filter that can hide a no-op ('Already up to date'). Script them with 'git -C $ROOT' on every call, and re-check an independent count (e.g. log-entry count, main's sha moved) before committing.
outcome: Recurrence 2: a cd'd merge chain merged a docs branch into itself, and 'grep CONFLICT' hid the no-op, so the branch looked merged while main had not moved. It was escalated as a process defect. The promised script (merge_three.sh) never landed, so the lesson stays live.

instruction: A 'main has not moved' assertion is '... || exit 1', never '[ ... ] && echo OK', because a miss prints nothing. Before claiming 'no baseline moved', diff ratchet baseline KEY SETS against main.
outcome: In REQ-021a the drift surfaced four commands later. A gate category that landed after the branch base made rc 0 'honest and wrong' on the composed tree.
enforcement: branch_health.sh baseline_widen_check.py flags LOOSER-THAN-MAIN; the '|| exit 1' half is still manual

instruction: Retire every merged branch: tag it completed/<branch>@<date>, remove its worktree and delete the branch. Refuse when the worktree has uncommitted files.
outcome: Merged branches stop interfering with future work. The refusal comes from lesson L-11, which this step did not open.

instruction: Agents USE credentials but never TYPE them: restore the saved session or use a gitignored, owner-supplied auto-login file. Never write a credential or PIN into a file or commit.
outcome: Hands-free authenticated test legs with no secrets in the repo.
owner_words: yes you have all my consent but always test on newer build , u can use login

instruction: Limit blanket test consent to disposable tenants or accounts. Never touch the live production tenant, and keep the newest-build rule in force.
outcome: Keeps the blast radius on throwaway data.

instruction: The owner performs all logins. Never handle or enter the owner's credentials.
outcome: A standing constraint; later relaxed only to the session-carry and auto-login file (#44).

instruction: Treat production project and database identifiers as frozen.
outcome: A standing constraint.

instruction: Never commit or push directly to the production branch; branch every change.
outcome: A standing constraint.

instruction: Gate destructive operations on tenant or production data on the owner: dry-run first, keep an audit log of the original bodies, and run in a quiet window.
outcome: A standing constraint.

instruction: Only the owner rotates third-party API keys.
outcome: A standing constraint.

instruction: Never let session-restore records carry admin-password material.
outcome: A standing constraint.

instruction: Relax no safety rule in outcome mode.
outcome: Speed never trades away safety.

instruction: Leave the remote CI workflow files unchanged so they resume if restored, but let nothing wait for them.
outcome: Reversible decision.

instruction: Bump the version in ONE scripted step that updates every version file together. Run the batch gate on the bumped tree. Any commit after the gate re-runs every test that reads what it touched.
outcome: Earned on the v20.4.0 merge train.

instruction: Before any check relative to the main branch, fetch origin, count how far HEAD is behind, compute against origin/main and report a non-zero count. If a trial merge-tree is clean, bring the base current.
outcome: Earned in D-PROC-3: checks against a stale local main gave wrong answers.

instruction: Before backing up or naming any captured environment or session archive, read which tenant or account it belongs to and refuse a non-disposable one.
outcome: Earned when a session carry was taken from the live tenant.

instruction: A rework running at the same time as a verifier gets its own worktree. The dispatch names that worktree and marks the verifier's tree off-limits.
outcome: Earned in REQ-023c, where a rework ran concurrently with certification.

instruction: Commit every artifact a later agent must read (judge reviews, plans) on the branch. Keep scratch inside the repo's ignored scratch folder, never system /tmp. Scratch holds only trial trees and transient probes, never a successor's source of record.
outcome: Per CLAUDE.md #32, a session resume recreated the /tmp scratchpad EMPTY, losing every judge review, the rig plan, a pulled APK and the merge resolver.
owner_words: Save the scratch pad and memory next time so that nothing is lost if there is interruption; only successful completion of a task removes all resources associated with it.

instruction: Merge in TRAINS: compose the branches with merge-tree, run one full gate per train, merge in order and retire each branch. A code train needs one go per train. Certify a debug-only code diff as INSTRUMENT-ONLY.
outcome: Per CLAUDE.md #45, the full suite once ran five times in one day for changes that never interacted.

instruction: Clear a script as 'read-only' by its writes per DESTINATION (production data, device, repo), never by its call syntax; a script that reads back its own effect is a WRITER. Never override a disposition your own card reserved for the owner.
outcome: Earned in rig hygiene.

instruction: Never run generator scripts that write a repo-global 'current feature' pointer. Write the per-requirement specs directory directly.
outcome: The scripts wrote a global pointer that every agent's feature directory resolves through. Concurrent agents clobbered each other (cf. lesson L-13).

instruction: Never checkout, switch, commit or merge in the main checkout; it stays on the default branch. Give your branch its own worktree and make every git call 'git -C <worktree>'.
outcome: REQ-025: a Developer's 'checkout -b' in the main checkout switched the shared tree off main and redirected the PO's next merge into the feature branch.

instruction: Never apply a mutant by hand to a file in a tree others read or commit. Every mutant runs through the mutation-battery script, which mutates a scratch worktree; if a mutant cannot yet be expressed as a battery row, write the row first.
outcome: REQ-322: a hand-applied mutant of a test helper was committed and pushed by a concurrent checkpoint.

instruction: A ref in a committed file must resolve wherever the reader is. Prefer a 40-character SHA that is an ancestor of the remote default branch; a local tag is not a pin. Check any durability a tool promises inside the tool itself.
outcome: D1b section 7.

instruction: A conflict claim is pasted merge-tree output, never inferred. A conflicting ratchet baseline is recomputed with --update on the composed tree, never by taking a side; re-check the totals and state the recomputed value.
outcome: REQ-086 and REQ-068.

instruction: Never run scaffolding scripts that write repo-global state (e.g. a shared feature.json). Write the per-requirement spec directory directly.
outcome: The repo-global .specify/feature.json clobbers other agents working in parallel.

instruction: Do trial merges in a detached scratch worktree (worktree add --detach main, then merge --no-commit). The branch tip, main and compositions get NO suite: cite main's numbers from the dispatch. Check siblings with 'merge-tree --write-tree --name-only' to a file.
outcome: #28 audit: a certifier's trial merge landed on main as a real commit and it carried on for 20 commands. Another certifier ran both roots on four trees (history agent-test-agent.md:373-386).

instruction: Assert main's sha is unchanged before and after every battery or trial-merge command. If main moved, stop and escalate in the same turn.
outcome: Same #28 incident: a trial merge landed on main unnoticed.

instruction: Never accept a code, password or credential LITERAL from a dispatch, and never write one into a file or commit. Treat any credential-shaped literal in a dispatch as a hint to verify.
outcome: BINDING [B-4]. Earned by P4-3, where a stale dispatched code nearly locked the till.

instruction: The device grant covers disposable test tenants only. The live production tenant is never installed over, written to or signed into, whatever consent says.
outcome: BINDING [B-5] (#44). Dev and prod share production data.

instruction: The device-test token is GRANTED by the dispatch, never taken. An ungranted leg is NOT-RUN. A device that is logged in or in the foreground belongs to the owner and is read-only (screencap, logs, dumpsys) unless the dispatch names it as the rig.
outcome: REQ-110: a wipe smoke ran on the owner's emulator under a self-taken lock while the owner was using it (history agent-test-agent.md:368-372).

instruction: As coordinator, stay read-only on the repo except the ledger, the context files and your own plan/verify records. Never commit product files.
outcome: Rules that bind the orchestrator. Unmeasured.

instruction: Never type a credential or access code, and never register a tenant or account.
outcome: Rules that bind the orchestrator. Unmeasured.

instruction: Never kill an emulator, the device bridge, or any process younger than ten minutes.
outcome: The watchdog only kills waiters older than 10 minutes (watchdog.sh:109). Protects the user's running devices.

instruction: Never push an agent's commit while that agent is still running. An agent's branch is its own until it hands back.
outcome: Cloud-onboarding session: the agent amended after the push, the branch diverged, and recovery cost a force-push.

instruction: Never run two WRITING agents in one worktree: one worktree, one writer. Read-only stages may share.
outcome: A ratchet measured under a concurrent agent was contaminated, and a shared activity-log file got swept into the wrong commit.

instruction: Before resolving a commit from paths (git log -1 -- <paths>), drop non-exclusive paths (the shared activity log, files other swarms edit), or have the committer record the sha.
outcome: D61: D53's resolver included shared files, so it would have scored the requirement's own mutation survivors as pre-existing.

instruction: Order file operations only inside the repo; stray files outside go on the owner-only list. Size a citation repair by listing every file:line the test guards, with its expected text, in one script run.
outcome: D142 ordered a deletion at the filesystem root. The harness refused it, so the bar was unreachable and the lane rightly stopped.

instruction: Never chain a check into the commit with &&. Make it an explicit gate that exits non-zero BEFORE the commit.
outcome: The commit ran regardless of the check.

instruction: Prompt hygiene: no credential, PIN or password in any prompt; no agent registers accounts or logs in with a password; no --no-verify; no rm -rf; every prompt carries the machine rule.
outcome: The skill says the launcher refuses otherwise. Note: product-pipeline:603 lets the PO pass a device admin PIN in a dispatch prompt, which conflicts.

instruction: While a workflow's train may merge in the main checkout, do not switch that checkout to another branch.
outcome: The train merges there.
enforcement: train prompt checks symbolic-ref is main

instruction: After a merge: retire the branch with the lifecycle script, regenerate the board, and make the ledger line the record.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: A step that touches git commits its own outputs with hooks active.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Append a dated section to the requirement's test report and commit it on the branch. Move the branch ref only if the tip is unchanged; otherwise rebase your commit.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Take the merge-train lock with an atomic mkdir and write the requirement and agent identity into it, never a pid. Wait in separate steps while another train holds it.
outcome: Near-miss 2026-09-08: a dead pid read as an orphaned lock, inviting a break of a live train's lock.

instruction: The train composes at main's tip in a scratch tree, runs the full gate once (analyzer, both test roots, all gates, policy check, battery) and a visual check for UI changes. It merges no-ff with gate results in the message, retires the branch, records state, then removes tree and lock. No version bump or build.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Before syncing a worktree to a branch a reviewer moved, 'git status --short' must be EMPTY; then reset --hard to the tip. Otherwise stop and report.
outcome: Protects uncommitted work.

instruction: The only permitted --force is 'git worktree remove --force' on a scratch tree you own.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Commit spec, code and the activity-log entry together. Tick device-verification boxes only on evidence.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Serialise merges through the orchestrator and re-run the gate on the merged tree. Green on two branches separately is not green on their union.
outcome: No measurement given.
enforcement: POLICY 11 blocks direct commits to main

instruction: Trip a run in the same turn on any of: a second suite on a non-main tree; any merge whose target is not the agent's own scratch tree; main moved; worktrees added minus removed > 2; turns > 0.8 x budget.
outcome: 2026-09-04: a certifier's trial merge landed on main and was pushed under the next docs merge (reverted with the full gate), and 60 scratch worktrees (18 GB) were live with zero removals.

instruction: A worktree sees only committed files. Contract dirs must show empty 'git status --porcelain' before 'git worktree add'; afterwards, ls the inputs inside the worktree. A missing input is a failed dispatch the orchestrator fixes.
outcome: Three REQ-030 input docs were untracked while the worktree was live.

instruction: Two agents never share a worktree, and no spawned agent writes in the main tree.
outcome: See the resource-deadlock item (SQLite fixture clobber).

instruction: Remove a worktree in the same step as its merge, and audit worktrees against merged branches at every heartbeat.
outcome: A worktree was found still on a merged branch, an unowned residual.

instruction: A test-only device PIN may be passed in the dispatch prompt but never written to a committed file. Account logins stay the owner's.
outcome: Owner directive #38. Conflicts with req-ladder:76-77 ('no credential, PIN or password value in any prompt').

instruction: Have agents work in a checkout passed in explicitly, normally a fresh worktree cut from the up-to-date main branch. The default checkout may sit on a superseded branch, and several work items cannot share one tree.
outcome: Earned by REQ-327 (2026-10-13): the default checkout sat on a superseded branch.

instruction: Tell every worker agent it must never switch branch, commit or push. Only the orchestrator, or a dedicated mechanical checkpoint step, touches git history.
outcome: Keeps parallel agents from colliding on git state. Concurrent commits are serialized separately (task-by-task.js:34).
enforcement: prompt text in BASE/PRE (not mechanically checked here)

instruction: Run mechanical tick-and-checkpoint steps one at a time through a serialized queue (two concurrent git commits would collide), and drain the queue before the run returns.
outcome: Prevents commit collisions between parallel lanes.

instruction: Checkpoint a long-running swarm's progress as WIP commits on the current branch (fast-forward only, tests and specs before the code they cover) so an interruption loses nothing.
outcome: A swarm writes files for hours, and container restarts or usage limits must lose nothing (#32).

instruction: Merge certified work as ONE train once the re-gate on the recomposed tip is green. Do not split ahead of time, because splitting only buys a second full gate.
outcome: Cited as the measured 'one gate per batch' rule (directive #45). Holding certified work off main reproduces the 53-stranded-branch class.

instruction: Block a dangerous release state with a script that refuses (non-zero exit, one line naming what is missing), never with a rule in prose. Ship the refusal with a RED fixture and a GREEN control.
outcome: The store build passed no defines, so it would have shipped a refusing sign-in card. The build script now refuses unless the key file is present.

instruction: When merging decision and activity logs from parallel branches, take the union and never drop an entry. Never renumber an id that is already cited. Renumber a lane-allocated collision only at the train and leave an id note.
outcome: Two D165s were kept and told apart by title. D373 allocated in a worktree became D375 at the train, with a note.
enforcement: proof: every '## ' header from both parents is in the result (comm -23 empty both ways)

instruction: A recorded decision judge GO is a legitimate merge go. Where nothing on the host enforces checks, the merger reads the check runs itself and merges exactly the named head with a merge commit, never a force-push. Fix contradictory lines in the instruction file in the same PR.
outcome: main had no protection and no required checks. CLAUDE.md lines 148-149 contradicted the new merge-gate item 6.

instruction: Off-path work started after the strict outcome rule is cut out of the merge tree hunk by hunk: not shipped red, not skipped, not waived. It stays on the working branch as a backlog probe.
outcome: An S5#3 test started after D315 was red on a fixture gap and was removed from the cut.

instruction: An owner's conditional GO is executed only when every condition holds on ONE tree sha: suite and second test root green, analyzer no worse, gates at 0, diff coverage, batteries with 0 unexplained survivors, final judge PASS per outcome, local CI green. Route it through a PR, never a direct push. The version bump and tag go in a separate commit.
outcome: REQ-306 merged by this route (D337 merge GO on PR #55).
owner_words: Once every thing as discussed above is fixed merge to main

instruction: Merge-gate 'suite green' is a property of the tree that lands on main. Cut a requirement-only tree from main carrying only its own paths. A red that is identically red on main is not attributable to the change, and another lane's red tests or residue never land.
outcome: The candidate PR would have landed other lanes' red tests and 160 tracked failure images on main.

instruction: Land parallel sessions in sequence: one shared process-and-tooling PR touching only scripts, config, instruction and doc files, then one fresh-cut PR per requirement carrying only its own paths, ported blob-wise. A sync-risk requirement never shares a train, so a regression bisects to one merge. Run the branch-overlap check before each cut.
outcome: Four PRs (169, 91, 77 and 7 commits ahead) were each unmergeable as-is.

instruction: Conflict rules for later merges: a stale copy of an already-landed file takes main's side wholesale, logs take the union, and any other file changed on both sides keeps the earlier landing's hunks and adds only its own.
outcome: Taking stale blobs would have reverted landed fixes.
enforcement: proof by blob equality per path

instruction: Compose ready cards into ONE train: one merge commit per card (bisectable and revertable), a policy check per merge, one gate on the frozen head, one PR, one version bump. Prove conflict resolution by counts (e.g. heading counts before and after). Re-run batteries only where a merge touched a shared file and cite the rest from lane shas. A failing card is reverted, not the whole gate re-run.
outcome: A gate costs about 17 min of baseline alone. A second gate would double wall clock and the bump for no added safety.

instruction: Resetting test data uses a script that asserts the target id, refuses the production tenant, dry-runs first and audit-logs the original records.
outcome: Ordered before a store re-capture on a disposable tenant.

instruction: The merge itself happens in the main session, never from a child session. Owner-only physical acts (signing, store upload, hardware legs) are named and batched, never faked.
outcome: Owner ruling recorded in REQ-322 merge decisions.

instruction: Report 'merged' by both ancestry and patch content (cherry-pick/squash aware), note which refs contain which so a stack merges once at its top, and predict conflicts with merge-tree.
outcome: A branch can be unmerged by ancestry yet empty by content, or the reverse after a revert; guesses lost changes.

instruction: When a new door lands, backfill honest events for pre-existing branches using only the branch itself as evidence; never mark anything merged, certified or passing.
outcome: 44 of 53 unmerged branches predated the ledger door and failed on a missing event though merge-tree showed zero conflicts.

instruction: Checkpoint a running swarm as fast-forward-only WIP commits; commit tests, specs and docs before the code they cover; when bypassing hooks, run the policy check on the whole tree instead.
outcome: Interruptions (container restart, usage limit) must lose nothing (#32); history never shows code ahead of its RED tests (J18).

instruction: Retire merged branches mechanically: tag completed/<branch>@<date>, remove the worktree, delete the branch, and refuse anything not proven merged and clean.
outcome: A certified verdict was destroyed irrecoverably by a forced worktree removal (L-11).

instruction: Prove 'merged' against origin/main after a fetch, never against the local main.
outcome: REQ-327: local main differed from origin.

instruction: Close an unmergeable branch without closing the defect: record a PARKED event naming the blocker and recovery tag, open a successor card for the remaining gap, then retire; refuse to park anything mergeable.
outcome: Silent retirement would drop real defects from the board; leaving branches open forever is the mess the rule bans.

instruction: Resolve bookkeeping merge conflicts deterministically (derived dashboards take main's; generated ratchet baselines are recomputed from the merged tree) and abort on any product conflict.
outcome: Of 52 unmerged branches, 15 collided only on hand-edited dashboards and 12 on a generated baseline; hand-picking a baseline side can describe neither tree.

instruction: Refuse a recomputed ratchet baseline that is looser than both parents at any path; a merge may inherit looseness, never invent it.
outcome: Unconditional --update would silently raise a floor to accommodate a semantic conflict introduced by the merge.

instruction: Check every mktemp result before use; ratchet the hazard by a set of file::var keys, not a total.
outcome: An empty mktemp result made git -C '' operate on the real checkout: a harness staged the whole working tree and moved HEAD to an uncreated branch.

instruction: Fail closed on any driver that can write production data; refusing costs a human one environment variable.
outcome: Nine drivers bypassed the smoke and lock; four tendered real bills on a live production tenant.

instruction: Automation must structurally exclude the owner's live devices/environments (excluded by port, kill only marked clones).
outcome: Protects the owner's running tills (never disturb devices in use).
enforcement: headless_rig.sh port exclusion; rig_boot.sh exit 2 refusal

instruction: Never move a release tag and never tag a guessed branch tip; create only tags absent from origin, push each by name, confirm with ls-remote, dry-run by default.
outcome: Cloud sessions are refused tag pushes (HTTP 403); a tag invented for an unpinned tip manufactures history (D25).

instruction: A ref written into a committed file must resolve from origin; a local tag is not a pin; prefer a 40-char SHA reachable from origin/main.
outcome: A script rewrote pins to local-only tags; 257 such tags existed in one clone and four batteries were red in every other clone and in CI.

instruction: Never checkout/commit/merge in the main checkout; each branch gets its own worktree and every git call uses git -C <worktree>.
outcome: Shared-checkout git operations collided across agents.

instruction: Never accept a secret literal (PIN, password, code) from a dispatch and never write one into a file or commit.
outcome: Test Agent BINDING.

instruction: Destructive tests run only on disposable tenants/accounts; the live tenant is never installed over, written to or signed into.
outcome: Dev and prod share production data.
